intro: You stand at the gate of Cappadocia. This is Tyana, an ancient city in Niğde province whose story reaches back to the 2nd millennium BC. A Roman city, with aqueducts and a sacred pool.
history: Tyana was built over the late Hittite town of Tuwanuwa, and under Rome it became Cappadocia's second city. It is also the birthplace of the philosopher Apollonius.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Roman aqueduct and the Spring pool, then the Mosaics and the Mound.
facts: Did you know? The spring that fed the aqueduct still fills the city's pool today. The philosopher Apollonius of Tyana came from here; his contemporaries credited him with miracles, and Rome long set him up as a rival figure to Christ. In the Hittite period the city was Tuwanuwa, and the nearby İvriz relief records the region's Neo-Hittite phase.
outro: This brings our tour of Tyana to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for joining us, and enjoy your visit.
